precepts.text: For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border. When Ammon caught our people, they slaughtered the pregnant women of Gilead, and God says he is not letting them slide on that. There will be a day of battle: and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together. Image shown in class: the leader of North Korea. I do not know if it is that particular man, but whoever is the leader in the land of Ammon at that time is going to be a prisoner of war; that is what the prophecy says, so look for it.
precepts.point: Then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?” Historically, when Gad was moved out of the land, Ammon moved their rusty butts into our land and dwelt in our cities. Amos tells what Ammon did to get there: “For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border.”

When they caught our people, they ripped up the women with child. They hung them upside down, just like the white man did to us, cut their stomachs so the baby fell out, and crushed the babies. That is what the Bible says they did, and why: they wanted to enlarge their border and take over our lands. They slaughtered Gad. God says, I'm not forgiving you for that; I'm not letting you slide.

“But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind.” Rabbah is the city of Jeremiah 49:2, where the Lord will cause “an alarm of war” to be heard. A day of battle is coming, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind: that's the Lord.

“And their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together, saith the Lord.” Put the leader of North Korea, Kim Jong-un, on the screen. Whether it is that particular man or not, whoever is the leader in the land of Ammon at that time is going to be a prisoner of war. That is what the prophecy says, so look for it.

precepts.text: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. That is what "Israel shall be heir unto them that were his heirs" jumps to.
precepts.point: Then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.” What does that mean? Romans 8 jumps right to it: “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.”

We are joint-heirs with Christ. Ammon made itself heir to Gad, inheriting his cities while Israel was carried away. But Israel is the heir of God, and in that day Israel shall be heir unto them that took his inheritance.

The condition is that we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified together. The suffering comes first, the inheritance after, just as Gad lost his cities and the Lord promises to give them back.

precepts.text: They of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead. The prophecy says God is going to give the land of Gilead to the tribe of Benjamin in the future.
precepts.point: Then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
The prophets show whose the land will be: “And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau”: we're going to own Esau. “and they of the plain the Philistines”: we're going to own them as well. “and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria”: we're going to get our lands back. “and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.”

The tribe of Benjamin, God foretells, will dwell in the land of Gilead. That is the land of Gad and Reuben and half of Manasseh, the same Gilead whose women with child Ammon ripped up to enlarge their border.

So the prophecy says God is going to give that land in the future to Benjamin. That is Israel being “heir unto them that were his heirs”: the land Ammon took is given back to Israel.

precepts.text: Moses had it mapped out: if the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan, then ye shall give them the land of Gilead for a possession.
precepts.point: Then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
Before Obadiah's prophecy, the history of the land: when we entered the land, Moses already had it mapped out for us. “If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan, every man armed to battle, before the Lord, and the land shall be subdued before you; then ye shall give them the land of Gilead for a possession.”

So you notice: Gad and Reuben, that was to be their land. Gilead was Gad's by the word of Moses. That is why Jeremiah asks, “why then doth their king inherit Gad”: the land was Israel's possession, given before the Lord, and Ammon had no right to it.

precepts.text: And the children of Machir the son of Manasseh went to Gilead, and took it. So Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh held that land. Map shown in class: Ammon sat right next to Gad, and when Gad was carried off, Ammon moved in; and on the modern map that whole area, spelled Amman, is what America calls Jordan today, in Arab hands, exactly as the history in Maccabees explains.
precepts.point: Then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“And the children of Machir the son of Manasseh went to Gilead, and took it, and dispossessed the Amorite which was in it.” So you had Gad, Reuben and Manasseh in that land. But in the prophecy of Obadiah, God says Benjamin shall possess Gilead.

On the ancient map you can see Manasseh, Gad under them, and Reuben under Gad, and right next to Gad was Ammon. When Gad was moved out of the land by the Assyrian captivity, Ammon moved right in. That is what Jeremiah 49:1 says: “their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities.”

After Nebuchadnezzar began to move them out, then the Persians, then the Greeks, the Arabs got the land of Ammon; the Greeks made a deal with them, as the book of the Maccabees tells. On the modern map it is spelled Amman, and that whole area is what America calls Jordan today. It is all Arab land, but it was Ammon and Moab's land, and before that it was Gilead, Israel's land.

precepts.text: And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other. We were scattered everywhere, and that includes, as we are finding out, China and Japan.
precepts.point: French art book of Nanban screens: black slaves in the Japanese paintings of the 1500s, carrying loads, rowing the boats, carrying the litters on their shoulders, the same thing we had to do for the white folks over here. Why are these books not in English in America? We had to go to foreign countries to dig this up, because they keep it secret.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

We were scattered everywhere, and that includes, as we are finding out, China and Japan. The paintings from Japan in the 1400s and 1500s show the black faces, and the black faces are slaves, brought over by the Portuguese and Spanish. In ancient China the Kunlun, African slaves, were given as tribute gifts during the Tang dynasty, and slavery peaked under the Tang and Song dynasties. The Portuguese brought enslaved Africans to Macau in large numbers in the 1500s, where they formed the core of its defense and defeated the Dutch in the Battle of Macau in 1622.

You don't learn this in school, and you definitely ain't going to learn it in Sunday school. They keep it secret and hidden. We thought these people were our friends; they had us as slaves too. That is why no nation wants to give us reparations: all nations got to pay.

This is how Israel came to be among all people from one end of the earth to the other, and why the question stands: “Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir?” The Lord answers that Israel shall be heir again.

precepts.text: The counsel against Edom and Teman: the least of the flock, the fake Israelis, draws them out into that land, the earth is moved at the noise of their fall, heard in the Red Sea, and he comes up and flies as the eagle over Bozrah, Jordan, America to Israel's rescue, and the hearts of the mighty men of Edom are as a woman in her pangs, because it is a trap and NATO turns against them.
precepts.point: An altar to the Lord in the midst of Egypt, and an altar is for sacrifice, the Israelites; they cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he sends them a saviour and a great one, Christ, who delivers them, the same as Jeremiah 30:7.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Joel says the Lord will remove the northern army far off and drive it into the land between the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean. Jeremiah shows what happens there.

“Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman.” Teman is still Edom. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: the least of the flock is these Israelis, the fake Israelis. That whole area on the map is where it is all going to go down. “Surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.”

“The earth is moved at the noise of their fall, at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea.” The ships in the Red Sea are going to hear about this fall.

“Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah.” Bozrah is Jordan, that area on the map. America is going to come to Israel's rescue, so they think. “And at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.” They are going to be afraid, because they don't realize it's a trap: NATO turns against them, and everybody is against America and Israel.

That is how the Lord takes the northern army down over there, while he tells us, don't worry, you are dying but you are not dead. Jacob's trouble is great, “but he shall be saved out of it.”

precepts.text: Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out: the counsel of the Lord against Edom.
precepts.point: The treacherous dealer dealeth treacherously, and the spoiler spoileth. America deals through sanctions, debt, spies and mercenaries.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“A grievous vision is declared unto me; the treacherous dealer dealeth treacherously, and the spoiler spoileth.” America is that treacherous dealer. An American economist who advised more than a hundred governments calls the United States the most lawless and dangerous country in the world, with CIA coups he saw with his own eyes and the Iraq war sold by a focus group in the Pentagon. It puts sanctions and embargoes on a country, kicks it off the SWIFT payment system, cripples its economy, and then pays protesters and sends Mossad and the CIA to stir up the people against their own government, as in Iran. It took out Gaddafi, who wanted to unite Africa on the gold standard and used his oil wealth for his people, and Libya is a mess to this day. That is how they deal: underhanded, with the CIA, Mossad, guerrilla warfare and mercenaries, as in Haiti, to monopolize the resources of all the dark nations.

Jeremiah shows the counsel of the Lord against the treacherous dealer: “Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Edom.” Edom in this context is the USA, America.

“and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman.” Teman is Amalek, the state of Israel. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out: surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.” The least of the flock is Israel, Amalek, and it shall draw America out.

So the treacherous dealer and spoiler of Isaiah 21 has a counsel of the Lord taken against it. The same Edom that spoils the nations will be drawn out by the least of the flock, and its habitations made desolate together with them.

precepts.text: A child of God is to accept both parts, the saving of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies.
precepts.point: This is our salvation and redemption. Every nation has held Israel captive at one time, not just the friendly neighborhood white man: the Assyrians, Babylon, Persia and the Medes, Greece and Rome, the many captivities in the book of Judges, the Arabs and Ishmael in the trans-Saharan slave trade, and America. Whosoever leads into captivity shall go into captivity.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

precepts.why:
“So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” A child of God is to accept both parts: the saving of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies. They come together.

That is why the word to Ammon reads the way it does. Both Moab and Ammon go into captivity, and both are promised a return, but the reckoning comes first. Afterward the Most High will bring again the captivity of the children of Ammon; the destruction of the enemies is what makes the salvation. This is our salvation and redemption.

precepts.why:
Balak king of Moab “sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor”, saying “Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me: Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me”. He hired Balaam to curse Israel and pull them into idolatry, for he said, “I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.”

That is who Moab and Ammon are to us: these nations have always been our enemies. So when the Most High says both Moab and Ammon go into captivity, it is because of what they did to Israel, and whosoever leads into captivity shall go into captivity. The reckoning on them comes first, and afterward their captivity is brought again. This is our salvation and redemption.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

precepts.why:
Now the word turns to Edom, and Edom is the so-called white man. Go back to his birth: “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Esau came out red and hairy; he is the one nation without the pigmentation the rest of the world carries.

This is not merely an Israelite interpretation. Bible dictionaries and encyclopedias confirm Edom points to the Romans, the Greeks, and the Americans. So when it says “Edom shall be a desolation: every one that goeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof”, as in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, and “no man shall abide there”, it is speaking of Esau, the red and hairy one, and the nations that came from him.

This is a very great nation whose fall astonishes the world, a people who almost ruled the earth with army bases and embassies everywhere. Babylon the Great, which is America, will fall; it is inevitable. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out: surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.”

He shall fly as an eagle and spread his wings over Bozrah, and that day “the heart of the mighty men of Edom” shall be “as the heart of a woman in her pangs.” This is our salvation, which comes only with the destruction of our enemies.

Every nation has held Israel captive at one time, not just the friendly neighborhood white man: the Assyrians, Babylon, Persia and the Medes, Greece and Rome, the many captivities in the book of Judges, the Arabs and Ishmael in the trans-Saharan slave trade, and America. Whosoever leads into captivity shall go into captivity.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: Edom shall be a desolation; everyone that passes by shall be astonished and hiss at all its plagues, as in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah. No man shall abide there.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: He shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan against the habitation of the strong, but the Most High will make him run away from her. For who is like the Most High, and who will appoint him the time, and what shepherd will stand before him?

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: Hear the counsel the Lord has taken against Edom: surely the least of the flock shall draw them out, and their habitations shall be made desolate. The earth is moved at the noise of their fall.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: This is a very great nation whose fall astonishes the world, a people who almost ruled the earth with army bases and embassies everywhere. Babylon the Great, which is America, will fall; it is inevitable.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: He shall fly as an eagle and spread his wings over Bozrah, and the heart of the mighty men of Edom that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pains. This is our salvation, which comes only with the destruction of our enemies.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: Concerning Damascus: Hamath and Arpad are confounded and faint-hearted, and Damascus waxes feeble and turns to flee, seized by anguish as a woman in travail.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: Her young men fall in the streets and her men of war are cut off in that day. The Most High kindles a fire in the wall of Damascus that devours the palaces of Ben-hadad.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar shall smite: arise and spoil the men of the east; their tents, flocks, and camels are taken, and fear is on every side.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: Nebuchadnezzar has conceived a purpose against the wealthy nation that dwells without care, without gates or bars. Hazor becomes a dwelling for dragons and a desolation forever.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: This word came against Elam in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah. Elam is the ancient and modern Persians, the so-called East Indians found in India, Malaysia, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, and Iran.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: The Most High will break the bow of Elam, bring four winds from the four quarters of heaven, and scatter them among all nations. He will set his throne in Elam and destroy their king and princes.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: Elam fell once already in the days of Alexander the Great around 333 BC, but the Most High says he will bring again the captivity of Elam in the latter days. When Christ returns, every nation will be subject to one government, the government of Israel given by the Most High in Christ.
